quotes.text: C++ is a horrible language. It's made more horrible by the fact that a lot of substandard programmers use it, to the point where it's much much easier to generate total and utter crap with it.
quotes.author: Linus Torvalds

quotes.text: There are only two kinds of languages: the ones people complain about and the ones nobody uses.
quotes.author: Bjarne Stroustrup
quotes.source: The Design and Evolution of C++

quotes.text: A language that doesn't affect the way you think about programming, is not worth knowing.
quotes.author: Alan Perlis

quotes.text: Any application that can be written in JavaScript, will eventually be written in JavaScript.
quotes.author: Jeff Atwood

quotes.text: Docker: because 'it works on my machine' wasn't a good enough answer, so now we ship the machine.
quotes.author: Unknown

quotes.text: No matter what problem you post on the internet, someone will suggest rewriting it in Rust.
quotes.author: Unknown

quotes.text: Why not use those providers directly? Does Cloudflare need to be in the middle of everything?
quotes.author: binarymax
quotes.extraction_note: Textbook grug anti-middleman instinct, stated in two blunt sentences. Kept as a rhetorical question because the question IS the joke — kept verbatim to preserve voice.

quotes.text: Create bot detection and bot protection, then sell crawlers. Is this the peak of hypocrisy?
quotes.author: sreekanth850
quotes.extraction_note: Sharp, funny callout of the business model contradiction: fence out the bots, then monetize the fence. Controversial, memorable, needs no context.

quotes.text: I've tried it, but I haven't seen anything that overly impressed me in terms of accuracy. I'm sure there are applications for LLMs where the quality of the answers is less important, but I don't have any of those.
quotes.author: jacquesm
quotes.source: Hacker News — Run Qwen 3.8 Flash Next (125B) on consumer hardware (RTX 4090) at 100T/s
quotes.extraction_note: Grug-brained skepticism of the LLM speed race — cutting through tokens/sec flexing to ask the only question that matters (does it work?). The closing 'but I don't have any of those' lands hard.

quotes.text: The property grid control is still the greatest general purpose UI of all time. Define your classes with some attributes and it just works. It was all downhill from there with web and mobile.
quotes.author: waldrews
quotes.source: Hacker News — A browser-native classic Visual Basic VB6 IDE
quotes.extraction_note: Genuine dev nostalgia with a sharp anti-complexity thesis: declarative UI worked, and the industry abandoned it.
